title: Comparative structural insights of X protein across species and the "lost" BH3-like domain that may explain the absence of hepatocellular carcinoma in birds.
authors: Kaur, Kuldeep; Beghin, Justine; Meier-Stephenson, Vanessa
journal: Infection, genetics and evolution : journal of molecular epidemiology and evolutionary genetics in infectious diseases
one_liner_zh: 该文用AlphaFold3和RoseTTAFold对哺乳与禽类乙肝病毒X蛋白进行跨物种结构比较，聚焦BH3样结构域缺失与肝癌关联，属蛋白-DNA互作边缘（X蛋白非TF-DNA体系），但结构建模方法可迁移至TF-DNA界面研究。
abstract: Chronic hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection is a leading cause of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). HBV produces an X protein (HBx) that is heavily linked to HCC, a similar finding seen across the Orthohepadnaviruses. There is an analogous, but truncated form of the X protein in Avihepadnaviruses, but no HCC is seen in infected avian species. This raises questions about the differences between mammalian and avian X proteins and their potential roles in carcinogenesis. Here we explore this question from a structural perspective of X proteins across mammalian and avian hepadnaviruses to determine whether there are any structural features linking these interesting observations. We first compile sequences to create consensus sequences with which to align with each other and subsequently to input into modeling programs, RoseTTAFold (RF) and AlphaFold3 (AF3). Comparative analyses show that mammalian X proteins are longer (154aa and 141aa, respectively for HBx and WHx) and have distinct domains in their C-terminal region, including a BH3-like domain that has been linked with many cancer pathways. Avian X proteins, however, are truncated with a similarly located stop codon. This truncation rids the protein of the BH3-like domain. We sought to find this domain by theoretical read-through or frameshifts and indeed, an analogous BH3-like domain is found that can similarly bind the BH3 target Bcl-2. Based on this work, it may be evolutionarily plausible that a single-nucleotide insertion led to the stop codon and BH3-domain loss that may account for the lack of cancers seen with Avihepadnaviruses.
abstract_zh: 慢性乙型肝炎病毒（HBV）感染是肝细胞癌（HCC）的主要原因。HBV产生一种与HCC密切相关的X蛋白（HBx），这一发现在正肝去氧核糖核酸病毒属（Orthohepadnaviruses）中普遍存在。在禽肝去氧核糖核酸病毒属（Avihepadnaviruses）中，存在一种类似但截短的X蛋白形式，但受感染的禽类物种中未观察到HCC。这引发了关于哺乳动物与禽类X蛋白之间差异及其在致癌过程中潜在作用的问题。在此，我们从哺乳动物和禽类肝去氧核糖核酸病毒X蛋白的结构角度探讨这一问题，以确定是否存在任何结构特征将这些有趣的观察联系起来。我们首先汇编序列以创建共识序列，用于彼此比对，随后输入建模程序RoseTTAFold（RF）和AlphaFold3（AF3）。比较分析显示，哺乳动物X蛋白较长（HBx和WHx分别为154个氨基酸和141个氨基酸），并在其C端区域具有独特结构域，包括一个与多种癌症通路相关的BH3样结构域。然而，禽类X蛋白因类似位置的终止密码子而被截短。这种截短使蛋白失去BH3样结构域。我们试图通过理论上的通读或移码来寻找该结构域，确实发现了一个类似的BH3样结构域，其能同样结合BH3靶标Bcl-2。基于这项工作，从进化角度推测，单核苷酸插入可能导致终止密码子出现和BH3结构域丢失，这可能解释了禽肝去氧核糖核酸病毒缺乏癌症关联的原因。
